comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C105-C108 regarding absence of neurodegeneration and overt inclusion pathology. Both evaluations support these findings, with peer reviewers specifically noting this analysis was added in revision and addresses prior concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C124-C138 regarding RNA-seq data and transcriptomic changes. Both evaluations support the gene expression findings and comparison to human FTLD-TDP data, with peer reviewers noting the use of multiple orthogonal endpoints as a strength.

Perfect agreement on claims C139-C150 regarding splicing analysis and Sort1 findings. Both evaluations strongly support the splicing data, with peer reviewers specifically praising the native TDP-43 splice target data and more robust quantitative measures.

Strong agreement on claims C85-C104 regarding behavioral phenotyping. Both evaluations support the comprehensive behavioral testing showing cognitive/behavioral impairment without motor deficits, consistent with FTLD-like phenotype. OpenEval also includes C58-C59 on viability which peer review addresses separately.

Strong agreement on claims C60-C64 regarding knock-in mouse model cellular phenotypes and splicing defects. Both evaluations support these findings, with peer reviewers specifically praising the use of endogenous models rather than overexpression.

Strong agreement on claims C2-C4 and C39-C50 regarding foundational rationale based on prior work about K145 acetylation disrupting RNA binding. Both evaluations support these background claims as appropriately referenced and establishing the study's rationale.

Strong agreement on claims C109-C118 regarding TDP-43 phosphorylation, insolubility, and biochemical characterization. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer review R6 also covers C119-C123 on spinal cord pathology which OpenEval addresses in R11.

Strong agreement on claims C72-C84 regarding hiPSC-derived neuron splicing defects including STMN2 and UNC13A. Both evaluations support these findings, with peer reviewers commending the native TDP-43 splice target data as excellent. Peer R3 also covers C65-C71 on microscopy which OpenEval addresses in R6.

Strong agreement on claims C51-C57 regarding overexpression data showing stress-induced foci formation. Both evaluations support these findings without challenge, with peer reviewers noting clear and convincing findings. Peer R1 also includes C5-C8 which are not in OpenEval results.

Strong agreement on claims C25-C38 regarding TDP-43 biology background. Both evaluations support these well-established prior work claims as appropriately cited. Peer R12 covers broader background including C1, C18-C24, C39-C43 which OpenEval addresses in R1 and R3.

Strong agreement on claims C13-C16 regarding the mechanistic interpretation and causal model. Both evaluations support the proposed mechanism linking acetylation to splicing defects to phenotypes, though OpenEval notes the causal chain could be more directly established through rescue experiments.

Agreement on claims C65-C71 regarding microscopy data in hiPSC-derived neurons. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer R3 covers broader hiPSC data including C72-C84 on splicing which OpenEval addresses in R7.

Agreement on claims C119-C123 regarding spinal cord pathology and early pathological events. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer R6 covers broader biochemical characterization including C109-C118 which OpenEval addresses in R10.

Agreement on claims C1, C18-C24 regarding epidemiological background and disease associations. Both evaluations support these established literature claims as appropriately referenced. Peer R12 covers much broader background context including TDP-43 biology claims.

Agreement on claims C17, C151-C152 regarding overall conclusions about the model. Both evaluations support the model's validity and contribution, with peer reviewers noting it replicates important FTLD hallmarks and avoids overexpression artifacts.

Agreement on claim C153 regarding the model's utility for future studies. Both evaluations support the model as a valuable tool, with peer reviewers noting it avoids overexpression and synthetic mutations.
